newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans Afghan talks with Iran and Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans Afghan talks with Iran and Pakistan.

text.p: Turkey said on Monday it planned to host talks with Iran and Pakistan next month on the fighting in Afghanistan.
"The trilateral meeting will aim to help parties in Afghanistan to come to an early and peaceful solution to the present conflict there," Foreign Ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news briefing.
The hardline Moslem group Taleban overran the Afghan capital Kabul in September. Forces loyal to Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani are now trying to win the city back.
Akbel said it was not yet clear who would represent the three countries at the meeting planned for early January.
He said the idea of the three-way talks on Afghanistan had originally come from Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Iran and Pakistan are among Moslem countries that Erbakan has visited since he became Turkey's first Islamist prime minister in June. His bid to form closer ties with the Islamic world has worried Turkey's Western allies.
Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is expected to visit Ankara this week.

A Foreign Ministry official said foreign ministers of eight Moslem countries, including Iran and Pakistan, would also gather in Istanbul in the first week of January to discuss economic cooperation and make preperations for a meeting of their prime ministers in early 1997.
